question.leadin: One of this organization's posters shows a cardiogram leading into its name.
question.text: Name this organization of union workers, led by Lech Walesa, that started a "self-limiting revolution". They protested at the Lenin Shipyard and various other places.
question.clue: The first prime minister elected from this organization spoke of the "thick line" that would demarcate his policies compared to the past.

swap.text: Solidarity was originally led by this man, an electrician who served as President of Poland from 1990-1995 and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1983.
swap.clue: This man mourned his successor in 2010 after that successor died in a Smolensk airport plane crash.

question.leadin: A radio mast in this city was the tallest manmade structure in the world prior to its collapse in 1991.
question.text: Name this capital city on the Vistula River. The most famous anti-Nazi Jewish uprising occurred in this city's ghetto, where the Muranow neighborhood was built after the war using "rubble-concrete" from the destroyed buildings.
question.clue: A forest near this city was the site of a facility built under Operation Reinhard in the village of Treblinka (treb-LINK-ah).

swap.leadin: Any member of this political body would immediate dissolve it with the words "I do not allow," the Liberum veto. --.
swap.text: Name this parliamentary body of an eastern European "commonwealth."
swap.clue: The szlachta class composed the majority of its Chamber of Deputies.

question.text: Sigismund II's inability to bear a child resulted in the formation of this personal union partitioned by Prussia, Austria, and Russia. Napoleon later revived a small part of it as the Grand Duchy of Warsaw.
question.clue: Monarchs agreed to the Henrician Articles and made individual commitments called the pacta conventa on becoming rulers of this country.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about figures in the Scientific Revolution.
swap.text: The Scientific Revolution is often said to have begun with the publication of On the Revolutions of Heavenly Spheres by this astronomer and proponent of heliocentrism.
swap.clue: In his most famous work, which he dedicated to Pope Paul III, he preserved the concept of "epicycles" and attempted to explain patterns of retrograde motion.

question.leadin: An underground trade union in this country went on strike at the Lenin shipyards in Gdansk ("g-DA-eensk").
question.text: Name this country. Lech Walesa ("lek va-WEN-sa") became this country's first post-communist president, but he lost re-election to Alexander Kwasniewski ("kfash-NEV-skee").
question.clue: Another man from this modern-day country fortified West Point, making Benedict Arnold's life difficult.

swap.text: This former capital and second largest city in Poland is home to the Dragon's Den cave beneath Wawel Castle. A noted cultural center, it houses Leonardo's Lady with an Ermine in its Czartoryski Museum.
swap.clue: Casimir III ruled from this city, which eclipsed early royal centers like Plock ("p'wotsk") and Gniezno ("g'nee-EZ-naw") after the pagan king Jogaila was baptized in its cathedral so he could marry the saint Queen Jadwiga ("yahd-VEE-gah").

question.text: Jogaila was the Grand Duke of what became this Baltic nation with a capital at Vilnius.
question.clue: Another Grand Duke of this nation signed the Union of Krewo to marry Jadwiga of Anjou.

swap.text: Algirdas's victory over the Golden Horde at the Battle of Blue Waters drove the greatest expansionary period of this polity, whose ruler Vytautus's involvement with the Samogitian uprisings and incessant warring with the Teutonic Knights helped prompt the Battle of Grunwald. For 15 points, identify this Grand Duchy which participated in the 1569 Union of Lublin.
swap.clue: This country which joined with its western neighbor in the 1569 Union of Lublin. In the 20th century, this Baltic state was the first to declare its independence from the Soviet Union.

question.text: Under the liberum veto rule, any noble could veto an act of the Sejm, the parliament of this country. The Union of Lublin united this country with Lithuania and it was later partitioned three times in the 18th century.
question.clue: Rulers of this kingdom agreed to a set of "articles" named after Henry of Valois, its first elected king.

swap.leadin: This polity incorporated the Duchy of Livonia into its realm during the Livonian War.
swap.text: Name this polity that officially formed following the Union of Lublin. This polity's Golden Liberty gave the liberum veto to all members of the Sejm ("same").
swap.answerHtml: Poland–Lithuania [accept either underlined portion; accept Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth; accept Grand Duchy of Lithuania]
swap.clue: This state lost one-third of its population during the Swedish Deluge, and this union formed after Duke Jogaila ] married Queen Jadwiga ].

question.leadin: A "general crisis" named for this century led to a population decline in Europe and possibly other parts of the world.
question.text: Name this century, in which both the Thirty Years' War and the Dutch Golden Age ended.
question.clue: 27 Czech leaders were executed in Prague's Old Town Square during this century, partially as revenge for an earlier event in which Ferdinand II's Catholic representatives were hurled out a window.

swap.text: This son of Augustus the Strong was the sitting king of Saxony and emerged from the war with both the Dzikow Confederation and the Treaty of Vienna supporting his ascension to the Polish throne.

question.text: This Grand Duke of Lithuania and later King of Poland converted the last pagan state in Europe, Lithuania, to Christianity, and then laid the smack-down on the Teutonic Knights at the First Battle of Tannenberg in 1410.
question.answerHtml: Wladyslaw II (accept Jogaila or Jagiello as family name)

swap.leadin: This man's forces were twice defeated by a brother of Egbert the One-Eyed named Wichmann ("VIKH-mahn") the Younger.
swap.text: Name this first duke and Christian ruler of the "Gniezno State" who was a grandfather of Canute the Great and a husband to Dobrawa. The Dagome iudex references this ruler's potential baptismal name.
swap.clue: This ruler who won the battle of Cedynia against Denmark. This father of Sigrid the Haughty may have performed one action to further his alliance with Boleslaw the Cruel.

question.text: The Swedish monarchy was much more powerful a century earlier when it controlled Poland from 1655 to 1660 in a period known by this name
question.clue: Key precipitating factors of this period include the increased power of the nobility due to Sarmatism and Golden Liberty system, and it saw secondary conflicts like the Second Northern War.

swap.text: The Essay on Diplomacy claims that nationalist movements would weaken Russia's influence, which this man supported with his "Prometheism" ideology. Czartoryski may have inspired this 20th-century Polish leader's plan to unite former Polish-Lithuanian lands into the "Intermarium."
swap.clue: This victor at the "Miracle of the Vistula" made formal overtures to fellow Entente members suggesting his nation should regain control of Danzig.

question.text: Boleslav was one of the great rulers of this dynasty which was founded by Mieszko I and whose other notable monarchs include Boleslav II and Casimir I.
question.clue: The semi-legendary namesake of this dynasty was a wheelwright who was legendarily visited by two angels in disguise who blessed his cellar.

swap.text: The Polish October also ushered in a huge worker demonstration at the Cegielski factories in this city in June, 1956. A 13-year-old named Romek Strzalkowski was killed during the protests. Much earlier, this city's namesake cathedral was the burial place for the first monarchs of the Piast dynasty, like our old friend Mieszko I.
swap.clue: A supposedly autonomous province of Prussia created after the partition was named after this western Polish city. Many early rulers of the Piast Dynasty are buried in this city's cathedral.
